display.purpose: Hero name only. One instance per page. The <em> inside is italic and Pit Lane Amber.

headline.purpose: Page-level headings on detail and about pages. Used once per page.

title.purpose: Stage card titles, prose H2. The primary working heading level.

body.purpose: All readable prose. Never use Playfair or Mono at body scale. Cap at 65ch in prose contexts.

label.purpose: Section labels, stage numbers, chip text, CTA button labels. Widest tracking — instrument register.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Stage card hover only. Fires with translateY(-2px). Never applied at rest.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Color and border-color hover transitions on links, buttons, chips, nav.

motion.name: standard
motion.purpose: Stage card transform, box-shadow, and radial gradient opacity.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: Theme toggle transitions on background and color. Radial gradient appearance.

motion.name: underline-draw
motion.purpose: Title underline draw via background-size animation on stage card hover.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Hero font size fallback, hero padding reduction.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Nav spacing, detail stats grid collapse to 2-col, about grid to 1-col.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Column border-left/right removed. Column goes edge-to-edge.

narrative.overview:
Every project is a chapter. The interface is the typeset book: Playfair Display carries editorial weight, Inter provides legible body text, and JetBrains Mono reads out the instrument data. The visual system recedes so the work can speak. Restraint here is not minimalism as aesthetic choice — it is restraint as professional signal. Decoration signals insecurity; this system signals the opposite.

The site runs on a single column bounded at 800px and ruled on both sides by a 1px border, like a logbook with a spine. A grain texture overlays the whole surface — so faint it reads subliminally, but present enough to make the screen feel material rather than rendered. The amber accent is used the way a status indicator is used: once, at the point of focus, meaning exactly what it says. Everywhere else is carbonized neutral.

This system explicitly rejects: marketing websites, SaaS landing-page patterns, gradient-heavy DevOps tool dashboards, generic dark-mode portfolios with teal accents and card grids, and heavy motorsport theming that reads as costume.
keyCharacteristics: Three-voice typography: Playfair Display (editorial weight), Inter (readable body), JetBrains Mono (instrument read-out)
Zero border-radius on every interactive element — angular throughout
Dual-theme (dark/light) with warm-tinted OKLCH neutrals in both modes
Grain texture overlay, opacity variable per theme (0.045 dark, 0.025 light)
Single chromatic accent — Pit Lane Amber — used at ≤10% of any surface
Column format: 800px max-width, vertically ruled by 1px borders

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Pit Lane Amber appears on ≤10% of any screen. It is a status indicator, not an aesthetic choice. Diluting it with color washes, section backgrounds, or decorative borders destroys its meaning.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Every text element is set in exactly one voice: Playfair Display (heading weight), Inter (prose body), or JetBrains Mono (instrument data). Mixing voices within the same semantic level breaks the register.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Hover Rule
rules.body: No static shadows. A surface casts a shadow only when it moves. If you find yourself adding box-shadow to a surface at rest, you are borrowing consumer app vocabulary this system does not speak.

rules.name: The Zero Radius Rule
rules.body: Every surface is angular. No border-radius on interactive elements. Softening edges borrows consumer app vocabulary this system deliberately rejects.

rules.name: The Watermark Rule
rules.body: Motorsport lives in naming conventions (stage numbers, logbook entries, status labels) — never in visual decoration, hero widgets, or oversize numbers.

dos: Do use Pit Lane Amber for exactly one semantic purpose per element: the thing that is active, selected, or actionable.
Do set body copy in Inter at 1.0625rem / line-height 1.75. Playfair and Mono are never used at body scale.
Do use tonal background steps (Column Black → Warm Surface → Raised Surface) to express depth at rest.
Do keep all surfaces at 0px border-radius. Every edge is angular.
Do apply motorsport naming texture to new content types — stage labels, logbook entry formats, status indicators — keeping it in labels and metadata, not visual decoration.
Do vary padding for rhythm. Flat spacing produces monotony.
donts: Don't build marketing websites, SaaS landing pages, or gradient-heavy DevOps tool dashboards.
Don't use the generic dark-mode developer portfolio formula: teal accents, card grids with icon + heading + text, gradient CTAs.
Don't apply heavy motorsport theming — no racing hero widgets, no giant lap-time numbers, no checkered visual patterns.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Headlines are solid Ink Primary or Pit Lane Amber, never blended.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, callouts, or list items.
Don't add static shadows to surfaces at rest.
Don't use the same padding value throughout.
Don't write marketing copy. The tone is logbook: direct, specific, no filler.
